title: GPU CI/CD Concurrency Scheduler and Cache Invalidation Playbook
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Summary:
This playbook documents the recommended architecture, operational runbook, pipeline patterns, and Terraform/IaC knobs we use at Redwood to coordinate concurrent GPU builds, manage limited GPU concurrency in CI/CD, and enforce robust cache invalidation for artifact and image caches. It is intended for infra engineers, build-platform owners, and SREs who maintain the gpu-builder fleet and pipeline automation.

Goals and constraints:
- Ensure CI pipelines make efficient use of constrained GPU capacity while meeting developer latency expectations (target: 95th percentile job start < 60s for incremental builds).
- Avoid cache poisoning and stale artifact/image promotion across environments (dev -> staging -> prod).
- Provide simple operators steps to recover from lock contention, cache corruption, and racey promotions.
- Integrate with existing services: buildkite-gpu-agents (GPU autoscaler), artifact-cache-s3, image-promoter, and terraform modules (gpu-node-pool, builder-iam).

Architecture overview:
- Components:
  - buildkite-gpu-agents: Fleet of ephemeral GPU builders that attach to Buildkite queues. Each agent requests a concurrency lease before starting a GPU bound job.
  - gpu-concurrency-scheduler (service): central lightweight scheduler that issues short-lived leases (token TTL 120s) keyed by queue and tenant. Uses DynamoDB/Cloud Spanner (depending on region) for lease persistence and optimistic concurrency.
  - artifact-cache-s3: S3-backed content-addressable cache with a TTL index maintained in cache-indexer. Artifacts are keyed by artifact checksum (SHA256) and build-metadata.
  - cache-indexer: background job that reconciles S3 objects and the index. Runs every 30m by default.
  - image-promoter: controller responsible for atomic image promotion via signed manifests and promotion-lock coordination.

- High-level flow:
  1) Agent starts, contacts gpu-concurrency-scheduler for N concurrency tokens (default N=1).
  2) If tokens available, scheduler returns lease_id and TTL. Agent proceeds to restore cache and run job.
  3) On cache write, agent writes artifact to S3 and emits a signed manifest entry to image-promoter queue. The cache-indexer updates the index.
  4) image-promoter performs a promotion step that validates signatures and acquires a promotion lock to avoid races across canaries and production.

Operational knobs (recommended defaults):
- Scheduler token TTL: 120s. Token renewal window: renewal at 50% TTL. Max concurrent tokens per tenant: 8.
- Max pending lease queue depth before backpressure: 100 per region.
- Cache TTL (S3 object lifecycle): 30d for artifacts, 90d for large model blobs by policy.
- Cache-indexer reconciliation frequency: 30m. Safety fence for deletions: 72h quarantine before permanent removal.
- Promotion lock lease: 5m. If a promotion takes longer, controller must renew in 60s windows.

Terraform/IaC patterns and manifest examples:
- Module: eng-infra/terraform/modules/gpu-node-pool (recommended inputs):
  - name: "gpu-builder-pool"
  - min_size: "0"
  - max_size: "40"
  - instance_types: ["p4d.24xlarge", "a100-40g"]
  - autoscaling_policies: "spot-fallback"
  - taints: ["gpu-build=true:NoSchedule"]

- Example terraform snippet to enable scheduler service and DynamoDB lease table:
  ```hcl
  module "gpu_concurrency_scheduler" {
    source = "git::ssh://git@repo.redwood/internal/infra//modules/gpu-scheduler"
    name   = "gpu-concurrency-scheduler-prod"
    region = var.region
    table_name = "gpu-scheduler-leases-${var.region}"
    lease_ttl_seconds = 120
  }
  ```

Pipeline patterns (Buildkite example):
- Job header: request token and set ttl renewal loop (bash):
  ```bash
  # request lease
  LEASE_JSON=$(curl -sS -X POST https://gpu-scheduler.internal/api/v1/lease -d '{"queue":"gpu-long", "requested":1, "tenant":"${TEAM}"}')
  LEASE_ID=$(echo "$LEASE_JSON" | jq -r .lease_id)
  TTL=$(echo "$LEASE_JSON" | jq -r .ttl)

  # renewal background loop
  (while true; do sleep $((TTL/2)); curl -sS -X POST https://gpu-scheduler.internal/api/v1/renew -d "{"lease_id":"$LEASE_ID"}" || break; done) &
  RENEWAL_PID=$!
  # trap to release on exit
  trap 'kill $RENEWAL_PID; curl -sS -X POST https://gpu-scheduler.internal/api/v1/release -d "{"lease_id":"$LEASE_ID"}"' EXIT
  ```
- Artifact upload uses content-addressable pattern with explicit checksum and signed manifest:
  ```bash
  CHECKSUM=$(sha256sum build/foo.tar.gz | cut -d' ' -f1)
  aws s3 cp build/foo.tar.gz s3://artifact-cache/${CHECKSUM}.tar.gz --metadata build-id=${BUILDKITE_BUILD_ID}
  curl -X POST https://image-promoter.internal/api/v1/manifest -d '{"checksum":"'$CHECKSUM'","meta":{"branch":"'$BUILDKITE_BRANCH'"}}'
  ```

Runbook: common incidents and recovery steps
- Symptom: builds fail to start, many agents stuck waiting on leases.
  1) Check gpu-concurrency-scheduler dashboard (Key metrics: leases_in_use, lease_wait_queue_depth).
 2) If leases_in_use ~ max_tokens and wait_queue_depth > 50, temporarily increase max_tokens per tenant by 1-2 while investigating (API: PATCH /admin/config).
 3) If wait queue grows rapidly, scale gpu-builder-pool up by +10 nodes via terraform/cli and monitor.
  4) If scheduler Saturation persists, identify runaway jobs (metrics: job_duration_p90 per agent) and disable offending queues.

- Symptom: cache-indexer reports index mismatch or cache corruption.
  1) Pause image-promoter (set maintenance flag).
  2) Run cache-indexer reconcile in dry-run mode: `cache-indexer --reconcile --dry-run --region us-west-2`.
  3) For mismatched entries, mark suspicious S3 objects to quarantine: tag `quarantine=true` and notify owners.
  4) If critical artifact missing, rebuild from source branch or pull from historical promotion manifest (image-promoter stores last 90d of promotion manifests).

- Symptom: image promotion race detected (multiple canaries attempt promotion simultaneously).
  1) Check promotion-lock logs in image-promoter. The lock is implemented as a short-lived DynamoDB entry keyed by image-name + target.
  2) If lock leak suspected (stale lock with expired TTL not reclaimed), run admin endpoint to force clear: POST /admin/promotion-locks/force-release {image}.
  3) After release, re-run promotion with strict canary gating.

Operational alerts and SLOs (examples):
- Alerts:
  - GPU scheduler wait queue depth > 300 for 5 minutes (severity P2).
  - Cache-indexer reconcile error rate > 1% over 10m (severity P2).
  - Promotion lock failures > 5 in 5m (severity P1).

- SLOs:
  - Scheduler availability: 99.9% monthly.
  - Artifact restore success rate: 99.5% over 30d.
  - Average incremental build start time (team-facing): p95 < 60s.

Operational playbook for capacity changes:
1) If expected sustained build volume increase > 30% for > 24h, coordinate with Capacity team to bump gpu-node-pool max_size and update autoscaler policy.
2) Schedule a canary autoscaling test using a synthetic Buildkite pipeline (tag: capacity-canary).
3) After the canary, monitor scheduler metrics and adjust token TTL or max_tokens per tenant.

Security considerations:
- Leases are bearer tokens signed using KMS. Do not log lease tokens.
- Artifact manifests are signed with our internal CI key; image-promoter rejects unsigned manifests.
- IAM: builder instances use a scoped role with least privilege for S3 put/get and DDB lease access. Rotate builder keys quarterly.

Dashboard and metrics to monitor (recommended Grafana panels):
- leases_in_use (by queue), lease_wait_queue_depth, lease_renew_failures
- agent_start_latency, agent_job_duration_p50/p90/p99
- cache-indexer_reconcile_duration, reconcile_errors_total
- image_promotion_success_rate, promotion_lock_acquire_time

Owner and escalation:
- Primary owner: infra/platform-build (pager rota: infra-oncall).
- Secondary owner: eng-sre.
- Pager escalation: 15m -> eng-sre -> platform lead -> CTO on P0.

Appendix: checklist for changing cache TTL or promotion semantics
- Notify teams and open a cross-team PR describing impact (7 days notice recommended).
- Run full-indexer dry-run and snapshot index state.
- Deploy change to staging image-promoter and run promotion smoke tests for existing artifacts.
- Roll out to prod with canary gates (10% of promotions for 24h).

References and links:
- Internal services: gpu-concurrency-scheduler, image-promoter, cache-indexer, buildkite-gpu-agents
- IaC modules: eng-infra/terraform/modules/gpu-node-pool, eng-infra/terraform/modules/gpu-scheduler
- Related docs: GPU CI artifact sharding, GPU image promotion canary playbook

Contact: Aisha Patel (aisha.patel@redwood.ai) — platform-build lead.

Change history:
- 2024-02-15: Initial draft created.
- 2024-07-03: Added promotion-lock troubleshooting steps and TTL recommendations.
- 2025-11-20: Updated defaults (token TTL -> 120s) and added SLOs and alerting thresholds.
